target_customer: Parents of children who need primary or urgent care and would otherwise use an ER or adult urgent care
problem: Parents face long, costly pediatric ER visits for minor problems. Brave Care runs kid-only primary and urgent care clinics backed by a tech platform and remote services.
business_model: Clinic visit revenue from insurance and cash pay, plus remote care services
product_category: Pediatric primary and urgent care clinics

founders.name: Darius Monsef
founders.background_notes: From his YC profile. TechCrunch July 2019 names him and Dr. Corey Fish as the launching duo.

founders.name: Corey Fish
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; TechCrunch says he wanted to build more pediatric urgent care clinics and needed a business partner.

founders.name: Maryam Taheri
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; TechCrunch calls her COO.

founders.name: Asa Miller
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; TechCrunch calls him CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: The core is operating clinics with a scheduling and records platform; the hard parts are operational and regulatory, not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Clinic experience and kid focus could be copied by hospital systems and urgent care chains; scale depended on capital for each new clinic.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mednax, owner of Pediatrix, led the Series B in 2021 as a strategic partner, so a large incumbent chose to partner rather than compete.

market_need_then: The company claimed visits cost about a tenth of an ER trip and took a quarter of the time, and reported an NPS of 92 across 10,000 visits in its April 2021 release.

branding.domain_note: Used bravecare.com per the YC founder profile (S19).

identity.mascot_or_character: Scout, with Otter and Penguin characters, per Brave Care's Dribbble posts
identity.visual_style: Brand guidelines posted on Dribbble describe a visual identity strong yet flexible across touchpoints
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful kid-friendly language such as The Brave Beyond

branding.brand_signature: Scout the mascot and kid characters

brand_strength.rationale: A developed kid-oriented identity with mascot characters, a federal trademark filed January 2021 and regional press, but no evidence it drove growth. The name is generic, and other Brave brands exist.

outcome_analysis: Brave Care raised a $10M Series A in April 2021 and a $25M Series B led by Mednax in October 2021 to open clinics in Portland, Austin and North Carolina. A single directory profile says all locations closed in December 2024 and that it had laid off about 40 people months after the Series A; no mainstream article or company statement was found, so the cause of the failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned. Capital intensive clinic expansion is a plausible factor but is not sourced.
notes: The shutdown date rests on one directory profile that cites a Hacker News post; Community Impact reported the Austin clinic closed January 8, 2025 (via an aggregator). Total raised varies by database ($35M to $43M); the three recorded rounds plus a possible seed total about $36M, and one outlet mentions a $5M seed that I could not confirm, so a gap may remain. The TechCrunch 2019 article states $1.45M raised in total, recorded as stage other because it does not label the round. Competitor list is empty because no source dated near the batch named rivals; one summary compared it to ZOOM+Care without a dated source. The Fish founder label comes from the YC page. Other Brave companies (Brave Health) are unrelated.
